findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the per-mutation HEAD-drift recheck and lost-lease abort_check() guards are preserved for coordinator-routed families (e.g. thread them through the injected execute adapter or wrap coordinate_and_fuse), since coordinator.coordinate() is pure and cannot host them.
evidence: Legacy _apply_batch loop: `head_pin = _recheck_drift(...)` and `abort_check()` run BEFORE each `_apply_one` dispatch (applier.py:660-663), aborting the pass on a competing reconciler write or a lost ref-lock lease.

coordinator.py docstring: 'Its DECISION logic performs ZERO I/O and reads no clock' — HEAD-drift/lease checks cannot live inside coordinate(); they must be threaded through the injected execute/locate or wrap coordinate_and_fuse.
The plan text names no mechanism for carrying these interleaved concurrency guards onto the coordinator route.
findings.finding: The plan does not specify how the per-mutation HEAD-drift abort and lost-lease abort_check() guards that the legacy _apply_batch interleaves between mutations are preserved once non-create families dispatch through coordinate_and_fuse.
findings.location: Plan step 2 ('Route update, delete, probe, clean-label, repair-property, and conflict plans through coordinator/fuse'); applier.py _apply_batch (:650-663), _recheck_drift (:697)
scenarios: A parallel reconciler writes to the tickets branch mid-batch: legacy would raise HeadDriftError and abort; a coordinator route with no drift recheck silently continues issuing writes.
The ref-lock heartbeat loses the lease mid-batch: legacy abort_check() halts; a coordinator route unaware of it keeps mutating.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the cross-project safety guard (bug 626d) and the per-mutation rebar-id audit guard are preserved on the coordinator route for migrated families, or that the coordinator path enforces equivalent pre-dispatch checks.
evidence: applier.py:631 raises CrossProjectTargetError BEFORE any Jira write to fail-closed on out-of-scope targets; applier.py:741 calls `_audit_rebar_id_label_writes` per mutation as the pre-dispatch authorization check.
The plan enumerates only the blast-radius mass-mutation guard (AC5) as a retained protection; it is silent on the cross-project and rebar-id audit guards that live on the legacy seam being rewired.
findings.finding: The plan does not state how the pre-dispatch cross-project safety guard (bug 626d) and the per-mutation rebar-id audit guard remain in force for families that now route through coordinate_and_fuse instead of _apply_batch/_apply_one.
findings.location: Plan step 2 / Acceptance Criteria; applier.py _apply_batch cross-project guard (:631-641), _apply_one audit guard (:741)
scenarios: A stale binding targets an issue outside the configured project scope: legacy fails closed; a coordinator route that skips the 626d guard could mutate the wrong project.
A mutation attempts an unauthorized rebar-id label write: legacy audit guard blocks it; a coordinator route that bypasses _apply_one's audit call would let it through.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the deferral-metadata lifecycle: who consumes retry_not_before, what re-attempts deferred work after it elapses, and how deferral records are retired/cleaned up so they don't accumulate.
evidence: 'Defer remaining matching plans with scope/reason/retry_not_before; let independent scopes continue.'
AC3: 'Matching remaining work is deferred with exact scope, reason, and retry_not_before'
ABSENCE: no plan text names the consumer that reads retry_not_before back, the trigger that re-attempts deferred work once it elapses, nor a retire/cleanup path for accumulated deferral records.
findings.finding: The plan persists deferral metadata (scope/reason/retry_not_before) but never specifies who consumes the persisted deferral, when deferred work is re-picked-up after retry_not_before elapses, or how deferral records are retired/cleaned up — leaving the shared-state lifecycle incomplete.
findings.location: Plan step 3 / AC3 — 'Defer remaining matching plans with scope/reason/retry_not_before'
scenarios: Deferred plans accumulate persisted metadata that no defined consumer re-picks-up, so matching work is deferred once and never retried — silently dropped.
Stale deferral records leak/accumulate across runs with no retirement path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a live/end-to-end acceptance criterion that exercises the newly-defaulted coordinator/fuse path against the real dispatch boundary (or document why the verified-fake substitute is faithful to production, or defer live exercise to a named child ticket).
evidence: 'Verified-fake batches assert wire order/call ceilings/tallies/logs/exit. Historical replay names any counterfactual stop...'
Step 1: 'change the internal operation-family default from legacy to coordinator'

ABSENCE: no live/end-to-end acceptance criterion exercises the defaulted coordinator path against a real endpoint; verified-fake and replay both bypass the live boundary, and no documented faithfulness rationale nor named child ticket defers live coverage.
findings.finding: This is a cutover that flips the default for non-create families to the coordinator path, yet the Testing section validates it solely through verified-fake batches and historical (offline) replay — no acceptance criterion exercises the newly-defaulted coordinator/fuse path live/end-to-end against the real dispatch boundary. The suite can go green while the live defaulted path is broken.
scenarios: The coordinator becomes the default in production but was only ever exercised through fakes/replay; a live dispatch difference (real endpoint failure fusing, real rollback re-observation) surfaces only after cutover.
AC4/AC6 close green offline while the real defaulted path behaves differently against the live boundary.

findings.finding: AC5 asserts legacy _call_with_retry nesting 'becomes UNREACHABLE for migrated families', but the impacted-sites section names only the _call_with_retry DEFINITION (dispatch_apply_phases.py:76) and batch_dispatch.delete_one.
